Intended use: Compare algorithms on a declared benchmark
What this audit establishes: Seven F665 versions share the same 665 negatives and 532/133 negative members; A4 and B1 also expose selection decisions in inspected code.
Direct observation and supported conclus: Within-benchmark scores compare algorithms against the assigned labels under their documented selection procedures.
Additional comparison for a broader clai: Test a new source or homology-aware partition with model selection outside the test set to assess transport.
References: Walsh et al., 2021; Kapoor et al., 2024; Cawley and Talbot, 2010

Intended use: Predict numerical potency under defined conditions
What this audit establishes: Binary F665 membership does not measure IC50 prediction error.
Direct observation and supported conclus: Milk-peptide QSAR work preserved useful ranking while numerical predictions deviated from measured IC50 values.
Additional comparison for a broader clai: Assess independent concentration-response errors and calibration under the intended assay conditions.
References: Nongonierma and FitzGerald, 2016; Zan et al., 2023

Intended use: Claim an added effect in a processed food
What this audit establishes: Sequence-level benchmark membership does not measure a food-matrix effect.
Direct observation and supported conclus: Yao et al. measured 29.2% inhibition in control biscuit digesta and 46.9% in cyclic-peptide digesta; only that comparison was significant.
Additional comparison for a broader clai: Attribute the incremental response and assess additional endpoints or human outcomes with corresponding experiments.
References: Yao et al., 2026; Tenenbaum et al., 2023
